newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end firm but off highs in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end firm but off highs in thin trade.

text.p: Italian stocks slipped from earlier highs but ended in positive territory in thin trading on Monday although the market was little moved by Wall Street's strong opening, traders said.
"It's a very dull, lifeless market. It closed up but volumes are very low, certainly not a positive sign," one trader said.
The All-share Mibtel index ended 0.45 percent up at 10,374 after a high at 10,422 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed 0.44 percent higher at 15,480 after peaking at 15,585.

Fiat closed 1.6 percent down at 4,375 lire in reaction to weekend comments by Prime Minister Romano Prodi throwing cold water over car industry hopes for incentives to boost flagging Italian car sales.
Energy group ENI was up 0.92 percent at 7,830 lire after a high of 7,900, helped by an 'outperform' rating from Societe Generale.

Carlo De Benedetti's stock did well. Hi-tech group Olivetti, the most traded share today with over 11 million shares, put on 1.04 percent to 515.5. Financial holding Cofide gained 1.25 pct to 810 and industrial holding Cir 5.85 pct to 924.6 lire.
Pirelli & C holding company stock rose 2.08 percent to 1,960 lire, again boosted by continuing market talk of a possible group restructuring.
Telecoms were firm, with mobile operator TIM up 1.13 percent at 3,582 lire. Banks were mixed, with Banca di Roma up 2.61 percent at 1,336 but Ambroveneto fell 0.84 percent to 3,657.

Insurances were mostly firm, with Generali up 1.24 percent to 30,201 lire on higher 1996 group net profit forecasts. INA ended 1.56 percent up at 2,081 lire after Swiss Reinsurance Co said it had built up a 0.75 percent stake in the group and announced its agreement to acquire INA's Uniorias unit.
